## Requirements

**One game model** (opened 2026-08-05). A client cannot always tell that a game has changed, because not everything it renders moves the game's `version`. This project makes every change go through one handler that moves one version, and redraws the application's design map around it. What is wrong now and why is in [`71-design.md`](https://github.com/delphside/programme/blob/main/applications/tile-lite-elite/3.1.7-changes/workstreams/application-game-architecture/71-one-game-model/71-design.md), *What is wrong now*.

**Seven work packages, deliveries decided per package** (D56, #442; WP G, #582, added 2026-11-11). The requirements below are folded into this project, not into its packages; the allocation is a plan, and packages may move a requirement between them during design. How the line between Core and Additional is drawn is in `71-design.md`, *Work packages*. Below the allocation are the code review findings routed here and the project's decisions; a new functional requirement is raised on this issue.

| requirement | package | why there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #253 no foreign keys | **#268 Core** | one migration while the model is open |
| #66 a rating point can link to a swept game | **#268 Core** | a DTO nullability question, while the DTOs are rewritten |
| ratings by edition, one rating per edition rather than across all (a bug: agreed 2026-07-22, never written down) | **#268 Core** | the rating key becomes `(player_id, edition)` in one migration with bots as accounts (D58, #444); existing ratings become English (International)'s, other editions start at 1500 (owner, 2026-09-26); the Stats view is #269's |
| #302 the snapshot has no schema version | **#268 Core** | it stamps the shape Core changes |
| #380 R8 one response header and error body | **#268 Core** | the contract Core rewrites (D65, #465); #402 fills the correlation id |
| #429 the engine concurrency setting is never applied | **#268 Core** | Core acquires `engine_limit` for every search and hint (D62, #462) |
| #449 R1 to R3 move input checked at the boundary, with property tests | **#268 Core** | Core rewrites how a move enters the game (folded 2026-10-18) |
| an invitation outlives its seat or its game | **#268 Core** (D67, #467) | aborting cancels pending invitations; seat messages are refused after the start |
| #142 reconnect catch-up, #80 a rename reaches others, #106 inviting yourself accepts, #105 withdrawing hides the game | **#268 Core** | true by construction (D67, #467) |
| #571 the code meets the 4.1.0 rules this project's design questions decided: RATE-4, GAME-12, ADM-2, GAME-11, ACC-6, RATE-5, NOTE-1, DEL-4, TIME-2 | **#268 Core**; NOTE-1, DEL-4 and TIME-2 to **#270**, beside #87 and RET-3 (#68) | each ends with a test citing the rule, or the rule changed where the code is right (folded 2026-11-09) |
| #572 a test for the engine move timeout | **#582 WP G** | ahead of #71, guarding today's timeout path until #268 replaces it (owner, 2026-11-11) |
| the design map: each kind of logic (game state changes, rule validation, persistence, the wire mapping, seats and invitations, scheduling) named with the one module and function that owns it, a procedure that starts a fix or change from it, and a check where one is cheap (only the single state-change point writes game state); and #428's Application & Game Architecture row | **#268 Core** starts it; each package adds its part | Core lays down the single points the map names |
| #157 a staged tile survives Remove and Abort | **#269 Core Client UI** (D57, #443) | the composition key; the two `fixme` cases in `e2e/tests/ui-state.spec.ts` are its acceptance |
| #152 removing a game clears the board and rack, #88 out-of-turn staging | **#269 Core Client UI** | composition behaviour (D67, #467) |
| #68 retention for games that never started | **#270 Additional** | a sweep rule, not a model change |
| #87 tell a player a message has arrived | **#270 Additional** | needs a notification route (Web Push) |
| #251 deleting a test account takes two ordered commands | **#270 Additional** | waits on #253 |
| #146 rework the play controls, #239 the board shows only the last move, #84 games list appearance | **#271 Additional Client UI** | not forced by Core |
| #73 undo, from a history keyed on the game's version | **#272 Undo and Redo** | its table is laid down in Core |
| #166 nothing happens when a move time limit expires | delivered in 0.9.0 | shipped with #400; the row goes when the diagram is regenerated |

Drawn from the table by `programme/scripts/board/roadmap-diagram.py --project 71 --write-issue 71`; where they disagree, the table is right.

### Code review findings routed from #460

The code review of 2026-10-02 found these in code this project rewrites; the detail is on #460, where each line is marked **→ #71**.

| finding | package | where the design answers it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a rejected exchange loses rack tiles | #268 | `71-design.md`, *A rejected message changes nothing* |
| a bot is never run after a timeout or a force-resign hands it the turn | #268 | *The engine is a client* |
| `game_moves` rewritten on every save | #268 | D61 |
| invitations survive an abort | #268 | `ApplyError::GameNotWaiting`; `71-functional.md`, *The game and its seats* |
| an unknown engine is accepted; an engine failure is answered 400 to the human | #268 | *The engine is a client* |
| `engine_limit` never acquired; the lock held across the search | #268 | D62; *Locking is per game* |
| a failed save leaves memory ahead of the database (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` stays on #460) | #268 | D69 |
| `/start` on a started game is a silent success | #268 | `71-functional.md`, *The game and its seats* |
| `create_game` validates seats inconsistently | #268 | one validation, in `apply` |
| the event stream exits when it lags and does not notice a closed socket | #268 | *One version, moved in one place* |
| single-game expiry announces a finish when the game goes on, and logs the wrong seat | #268 | sweeps go through `apply` |
| `suggest_move` re-implements the engine's pick | #268 | *The engine is a client* |
| a viewer's access is one seat (GAME-4) | #268 | *Access is a set of seats* |
| admin and invitation paths race between lock and database | #268 | *Locking is per game*; D70 |
| invitation status strings in four files | #268 | an enum, with the seat state |
| `MoveRecordDto.move_type` is a string | #268 | `71-data-model.md` §2 |
| misplaced comments in `game_state.rs` | #268 | the file is rewritten |
| no test of an engine timeout or panic, or of GAME-4 | #268 | `71-test-approach.md` |
| opening or removing a game leaves composer and socket state behind | #269 | *Stop clearing; start matching* |
| a slow response for one game reopens it after another is open | #269 | `should_apply` |

### Decisions

Each closes once applied, and the design cites it where it states the conclusion. Answered in order: document structure, functional, technical, delivery planning.

| decision | question | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #472 D71 | how the design documents are structured | one file per stage, a section and a test file per package |
| #442 D56 | two work packages or six | six, deliveries decided per package |
| #443 D57 | where the staged-tile fix (#157) goes | #269, by the composition key |
| #444 D58 | the rating key, for editions and bots | both in #268, one migration |
| #445 D59 | whether unique email changes how an invitation binds | superseded by D72 |
| #446 D60 | whether #71 carries #402's correlation id | no, #402 owns it |
| #468 D68 | what aborting does to seats with no player | frozen as they stand |
| #466 D66 | whether bot sessions are exempt from ACC-1 | no exemption |
| #479 D72 | how an emailed invitation behaves once an address identifies one account | the ten principles; INV-1 to INV-8 |
| #461 D61 | whether Core writes an append-only log | yes, `game_events` |
| #462 D62 | what bounds parallel engine searches | `engine_limit`, searches and hints |
| #465 D65 | the standard response header and error body | #268 designs it, #402 fills the correlation id |
| #469 D69 | what a failed save leaves in memory | a change exists once saved; a failed save reloads |
| #470 D70 | who owns the games map | #268; #408 builds on it |
| #463 D63 | whether #10's harness is a work package here | no: #10 follows #268, which builds the test client |
| #464 D64 | branches and milestones per delivery | `release/1.0.0` for #268 and #269, every schema change in it |
| #467 D67 | where the unallocated requirements go | where the design makes each true |

## Design

In the [`71-one-game-model`](https://github.com/delphside/programme/tree/main/applications/tile-lite-elite/3.1.7-changes/workstreams/application-game-architecture/71-one-game-model) folder in `delphside/programme`: `71-functional.md` (use case, journeys, lifecycles), `71-design.md` (overall, then a section per package), `71-data-model.md`, `71-life-histories.md` (WP A's entity/event matrix, #542), `71-impact.md`, the design map change `71-map-change.md` and its drawing `71-map-diagrams.md`, and the reviews. `71-handover.md` says what is open.

## Non-functional design

`71-design.md`, *Non-functional design*: capacity, failure, limits and timeouts, secrets and access.

## Test approach

`71-test-approach.md`, with `71-test-wp-a.md` to `71-test-wp-f.md` per package.

## Dependencies and related work

The generated header above lists what this waits on and what needs it.

- **#10 bot client harness** stays its own project and follows #268 (D63).
- **#439 player interactions** owns unique and verified addresses; D72 builds on them without waiting.
- **#538 move generator** is its own project; WP A's engine design depends only on its interface.
- **Anything game-related outside #71 is independent of it** (`71-design.md`, *Work packages*): #291 capacity and #296 account states each say so on their own issue.
- **Outside it**: #103, the browser tab icon, and any client change unrelated to games.
